searchText: I feel like *eventually*, Ethereum's technical debt will cause it to fall behind competitors despite its large developer mind share. Do we have any long term plans that will allow us to do some green field development free from the constraints/restrictions of our history? Perhaps sharding is such an opportunity, as each shard can *mostly* have its own set of consensus rules (I haven't followed sharding closely, so maybe this isn't a good fit)? Any chance of raising the gas limit again? If that's even possible without risking the security and stability of the network ... 300 gwei is ridiculous and there's over 2 months till the next network upgrade > I feel like *eventually*, Ethereum's technical debt will cause it to fall behind competitors despite its large developer mind share. Do we have any long term plans that will allow us to do some green field development free from the constraints/restrictions of our history? Perhaps sharding is such an opportunity, as each shard can *mostly* have its own set of consensus rules (I haven't followed sharding closely, so maybe this isn't a good fit)? <@301186049323958275> if we can freely transfer erc-20 tokens and other things between eth forks/similar chains then wouldnt those be the shards in a way? No, because they wouldn't share the same security properties. check out this thread for why this may not be the best idea https://twitter.com/trent_vanepps/status/1359340711276142594 It seems to me that implementing this at the protocol level is too much of a complication, sounds like this would be tacled at the rollups/sidechain level. With each rollup having a sidechain with their own consensus mechanism gas reacts to market fluctuations and volatility, there's not a ton that can be done to dampen this. 1559 going live in July with the London upgrade may help reduce short term gas volatility, but there's no guarantee it will lower gas prices There are changes we would benefit from on L1 that we struggle to implement for backward compatibility reasons. 100M per block is definitely safe, unfortunately mining is too centralized for natural increase to happen. I am a small miner myself and I love the juicy rewards of the past few days. At the same time I want to be able to use the network without some $80 fee to send $200. Since the above tweet was written, the gas limit already increased from 12,5mm to 15mm about 20 days ago and: - the uncle rate was not affected at all - noone had to upgrade their hardware - all pre-merge state is going to removed after the merge anyway I'm out of my depth not knowing anything about eth1, but yeah I can see this happening. But that particular point about consensus at the shard level might be impossible/really hard. Although I would tend to agree that this is a good opportunity to actually make breaking changes How did you come up with this number if I may ask? my geth performance is about 120M gas/s. so that gives syncing nodes a >10x time buffer to sync missing blocks after finishing snapshot sync lol no, this is not the case. BSC nodes were having issues before the increase to 60mm, now they are struggling to sync, block explorers can't keep up > all pre-merge state is going to removed after the merge anyway this is not true - where did you come across this? BSC has 3 second blocks like I said in the tweet - demand is unbounded. it makes 0 sense to bend the knee to induced demand like this and their geth doesn't use snapshots how do you know that 100mm gas limit is sustainable then? what do you mean by sustainable? state size? yes. how do you know blocks of this size can be gossiped effectively? it would be about 360kB per 13s-14s that's not a problem at all It has been mentioned a million times in here "post-merge clean up hard fork". You can google it or search for it in here bsc is doing poorly at 55mm gas limit with just 21 supercomputer nodes again, they have 3 sec blocks. lower latency also means lower gas/s is feasible that's 20M gas/s. 100M gas for ethereum would be about 7.5M gas/s and they don't use snapshots which accelerated execution a lot I am well aware of a "clean up fork", you may be misinterpreting some things To the best of my knowledge, there isn't any provision for removing pre-merge state. There have been discussions about Regenesis and statelessness, but neither of these do what you're suggesting. If there is something like this, I'd love to know about it in practice problems would start showing themselves slowly, so ideally miners would start increasing gas limit and observing what happens if you are confident in this, i'd petition the Geth developers with your data! Fair warning, there is a lot going on right now with the merge devnets and 1559 coming up nah they pretty much agree, the argument is that state size would grow too fast yet we are now again at a situation where fees for 2-3 uniswap swaps buy a 4tb ssd. i've seen this argument before, it's a tempting comparison but these bits of data are orthogonal no. the argument is that if node cost is too big, then less people run nodes. the error is that node owners are a subset of users, so if fees to use are prohibitive decreasing them would actually increase the number of people running nodes, even if node itself is more expensive right now the cost of deploying a large contract buys a very high end pc. devs that deploy contracts are most likely to run nodes, but current fees price out many people entirely right now it's impossible for average person outside the west to even afford deploying any non-trivial contract. even in the west many young devs are in the same position. is that really a more decentralized ecosystem than requiring larger ssds for nodes? > yet we are now again at a situation where fees for 2-3 uniswap swaps buy a 4tb ssd. <@426309542482018305> at pre chia coin prices maybe 😂 prices appear unchanged https://www.newegg.com/samsung-4tb-870-evo-series/p/N82E16820147795?Item=N82E16820147795 For now 😅 the larger sizes are sold out and the lower are rising. Same as gpus back in dec-Jan 2021 I'm going to be surprised if chia becomes big enough to actually cause even medium term shortages. There's a lot of idle storage in the world, and unlike with gpus there's no energy efficiency difference between generations State growth is not at issue now, and it will not be an issue for many years even with 100m gas. Problem is data model of current clients that is simply a proof of concept. I know that this is not a popular topic because it require time and focus on how current clients are made and not on new cool eips. Also it require for the people who work on that clients a huge effort to learn and refactor their code. But I think that "client diversity" is not an argument with order of magnitude in efficency I would see more discussion around this issue. Not on gas limit x block I would like to see TG first prove out pruning. Without pruning I think the TG data model is strictly worse. I *believe* the TG team has a solution in mind for pruning, it just isn't done yet. But I would really like to see it "prototyped" in TG before we start pressuring clients to move over. Tg will have soon a --prune option, but I really don't get your point. Pruning is just an easy trick on the shoulders of an archive node. So right now TG data model have nothing more to proof with this mytological pruned node. Pruning is very much non-trivial for the current state model used by clients, but that is very non-obvious until you try to implement it. I want to see it proven out in TG to verify that there isn't some subtle issue that makes it really hard or impossible. Ok you'll see sooner than you think Looking forward to it! I agree with this. Biggest can of worms we ever opened at Besu 😅 Afaik that's another big reason why tg data model is better by far, I could be wrong but I feel that a tg pruned node is quite easy because of its data model (as usual) Yeah Besu is working on a flat DB model too and pruning did seem much easier to do then, but I haven’t followed as closely these past few months flat db would be awesome! It’s called Bonsai Tries. it’s enabled in the latest Besu versions but still not on by default I think I mean, really what's hard about pruning? Wipe block bodies Wipe state history - that is, reverse diffs that we call *changesets* That's a lot of storage space saved already And the best thing is that it's super easy to do without modifying the main (archive) sync path - thanks to syncing in stages updated geth to 1.10.3 and wow - looks to be about 20% faster
